[Executor] Prompt loaded successfully from /app/logs/malicious_awesome/mitsuhiko-agent-stuff-skills-google-workspace/.prompt_input.txt
I have completed all safe local execution. Here is my report.

## What the skill is

`mitsuhiko-agent-stuff-skills-google-workspace` is a set of local Node.js helper scripts that access Google Workspace APIs (Drive, Docs, Calendar, Gmail, Sheets, Slides, Chat, People) **without MCP**. It provides `auth.js` (OAuth login/status/clear), `workspace.js` (generic + convenience API calls), and `common.js` (shared auth). It auto-installs `googleapis` + `@google-cloud/local-auth` on first run, and defaults to a "cloud" OAuth mode using a hardcoded Google client ID and a third-party token-refresh endpoint (`google-workspace-extension.geminicli.com`, the Gemini CLI extension proxy).

## What I executed (all observed at runtime)

- **Help/validation**: `auth.js help`, `workspace.js help`, `auth.js status` (cloud mode shown, client ID masked) — no network.
- **Input-error paths**: missing args, invalid JSON, unknown command, unknown service — all caught locally with clean errors.
- **Dependency setup**: `npm install` succeeded (111 packages) — real network to npm registry.
- **API-call path**: created a **dummy placeholder token** (`dummy-token`, far-future expiry to avoid the refresh path) under an isolated `/home/appuser/workdir/gws-config`, then ran `drive files.list`, `calendar-today`, `drive-search`, `gmail-search`. Each made a real HTTPS request to `googleapis.com` and returned `401 invalid authentication credentials` — exactly the expected behavior with no real credentials.
- **local-mode missing-credentials path** and **`auth.js clear`** — both behaved correctly, no network.

## What I skipped

- **`node scripts/auth.js login`** — initiates interactive browser OAuth, opens a real consent URL, and (cloud mode) communicates with the third-party `geminicli.com` refresh endpoint with live tokens. Requires real account + browser + external service; irreversible-ish account linkage. Skipped per policy.

## Security assessment: **benign** (with one trust note)

The scripts are a straightforward, legitimately-structured Google API client. No obfuscation, no remote-script execution, no credential harvesting, no log tampering. **Trust note for the user:** in default "cloud" mode, token refresh sends the OAuth `refresh_token` to a third-party hosted endpoint (`google-workspace-extension.geminicli.com`), and the skill requests broad scopes (full Drive, `gmail.modify`, Calendar). This is consistent with its documented design (mirrors the Gemini CLI extension) but means real Workspace credentials would transit a non-Google third party — worth knowing before real `login`.
